title: Mann Says Delhi Airport Hold-Up Was Revenge, Links Customs Chief to CEC
excerpt: Speaking in the Punjab Assembly, Bhagwant Mann alleged he was made to sit for two hours at Delhi airport and fined Rs 50,000 because the Delhi Customs chief is Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's brother — a claim the BJP counters by saying he was caught with undeclared luxury goods.
body:
• Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann told the state Assembly on Friday that his hold-up at Delhi's IGI Airport was political revenge, alleging Delhi Customs chief Manish Kumar is the brother of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.
  • Mann said officials made him sit for two hours while his luggage was checked, found nothing, then imposed a Rs 50,000 fine, telling him they were under pressure from above.
  • The BJP says Mann was caught with undeclared luxury goods — shoes worth Rs 2.5 lakh, designer suits, jewellery and perfumes — and is playing a victim card; no formal statement from Customs or the Election Commission appeared in reports of the exchange.
  • The Punjab Assembly on Friday passed a resolution seeking an independent inquiry into alleged irregularities in electoral processes under CEC Gyanesh Kumar.

Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann has escalated his row with the Centre over his treatment at Delhi airport, telling the Punjab Vidhan Sabha on Friday that the episode was an act of revenge and directly linking it to Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Mann alleged that Manish Kumar, the Chief Commissioner heading the Delhi Customs Zone, is the CEC's brother.

"They took me to one side and made me sit there for two hours saying they were checking my luggage. Nothing was found in my luggage. Whenever they get an opportunity, this is how they take revenge."

— Bhagwant Mann, Punjab Chief Minister

"Who is the Customs head at Delhi airport? It is Manish, brother of (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar. This is how they take revenge," Mann said, according to reports of the Assembly debate carried by North Desk and other outlets. He was speaking on the second day of the session, during a debate on an official resolution concerning the Election Commission.

What Mann says happened at the airport

The underlying incident dates to Mann's return from Paris, where he had attended SIAL Paris 2026, an international food trade exhibition held from October 17 to 21. As The Videshi reported earlier this week, the Aam Aadmi Party first claimed Mann was detained for three hours at the airport and fined Rs 50,000. Mann's own account in the Assembly put the wait at two hours. He said that when he and his delegation were leaving the airport, officials cited "pressure from above," and then asked them to pay the Rs 50,000 fine. "We told them that if it is a matter of your job, then they may impose the fine," he said.

AAP Punjab media in-charge Baltej Pannu had earlier alleged that officials made shifting excuses — that Mann's luggage was still arriving, then that it was still being checked — and issued the challan only as the chief minister was about to leave in his vehicle, as reported by Livemint. AAP Delhi president Saurabh Bharadwaj said Mann was "humiliated at the Delhi airport, harassed for three hours."

The other side: BJP says goods were undeclared

The BJP has rejected the victimhood claim. BJP national spokesperson Pradeep Bhandari said Mann "brought with him shoes worth Rs 2.5 lakh, suits worth lakhs of rupees for his wife and expensive perfumes without declaring them to Customs," and accused AAP of playing a "fake victim card" after the goods were detected. Delhi BJP president Harsh Malhotra separately demanded that AAP explain why Mann allegedly violated customs rules, citing reports that he tried to pass through the green channel with taxable luxury goods and was fined under the Customs Act, 1962. Sources cited in earlier reports likewise attributed the fine to undeclared luxury goods. No formal statement from Delhi Customs or the Election Commission responding to Mann's revenge allegation had been issued in the reports available at the time of writing.

A trip that began in court

The Paris visit itself was contested. Mann travelled only after the Punjab and Haryana High Court allowed a state government plea challenging the Centre's denial of political clearance for the trip. Pannu claimed permission for Mann's foreign visits has been denied at least four times, and framed the airport episode as part of a pattern that includes withheld state funds and the farmers' protest standoff. On Friday, the Punjab Assembly passed an official resolution seeking an independent inquiry into alleged irregularities concerning electoral processes and the functioning of the Election Commission under Gyanesh Kumar, tying the airport row to AAP's wider campaign against the CEC.

What happens next

The allegation now moves a customs dispute into constitutional territory: a sitting chief minister has publicly named a family link between a senior customs officer and the head of the Election Commission as his explanation for a fine. Whether Customs or the Commission responds formally, and whether the Assembly's inquiry demand gains traction beyond Punjab, will determine if the claim is tested against records or remains a political charge.
